reason: Conversation 2 covered the sensible checks in one pass, respected the no-DIY boundary, kept the diagnosis honestly uncertain between the mains suppression filter and the PCB, and pointed him to warranty/Candy-Haier service and an engineer; its only weakness is leaning a bit hard on 'call your insurer first' for presumed surge damage. Conversation 1 was inefficient and repetitive (asking him to unplug twice and to test a socket he had already tested), framed the model-number request around finding a 'repair part', and ended with a fairly confident 'control PCB / wiring' heading while never raising the possible extended warranty, though it did at least send him to an engineer rather than selling a board.
